title: AntiFox Targeting AWS Credentials: The Latest Wave of AI Agent Attacks
content_md: TL;DR The hacking agent got a sequel in under a week : AntiFox, a fork of ARTEX, now points the same agentic playbook at AWS. Hundreds of API requests in about 30 minutes were enough to reach production secrets. It does not even need a secrets scanner : Only 4 of roughly 45 attack frameworks ship one, yet an ARTEX build with none found 8 of 9 planted credentials, starting in under 13 seconds. Deleting a leaked key fixes nothing : The access lives on until you revoke it. Learn the Detect, Remediate, Prevent moves that shrink what a machine-speed attacker can find. Last week, Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported attackers using ARTEX, an agentic AI framework, to find exposed credentials on GitHub and abuse them to access cloud environments. Now, less than a week later, BleepingComputer reports attackers using another agentic framework called AntiFox to target AWS environments. AntiFox began as a fork of ARTEX, and researchers at Arctic Wolf have linked infrastructure running the framework to real intrusions involving credential theft and unauthorized cloud access. The attackers used this offensive agentic framework to compromise web applications, steal configuration data, and use any valid AWS identities it could find. In one intrusion, attackers generated hundreds of AWS API requests in approximately 30 minutes. Most requests were denied, but some succeeded, including operations that exposed production secrets.
